findings.text: In the already-installed branch, `local EXIT_CODE` is empty unless `NVM_UPGRADE_NPM=1`. The new guards use `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]`, which with an empty value gives an 'integer expression expected' error and evaluates false. As a result, `nvm install <already-installed-version>` never installs default packages, never runs `reinstall-packages` for `--reinstall-packages-from`, and never creates `--alias`. The guards are also inverted: they should be `-eq 0`, so a failed npm upgrade (non-zero) would trigger the next step.

The alias step is guarded by `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ] && [ -n "${ALIAS-}" ]`. When EXIT_CODE is empty, the test errors and is false. When every earlier step succeeded (EXIT_CODE=0), it is also false. So `nvm install X --alias=foo` on an already-installed version never creates the alias, and `return $EXIT_CODE` then returns an empty or stale status.

`nvm_install_default_packages` assigns to `EXIT_CODE` without declaring it local, so it overwrites the caller's or the shell's global `EXIT_CODE`. Callers other than `nvm install` get this variable clobbered. If the function is invoked outside `nvm()`, which declares its own local, the variable leaks into the user's shell.
